newsitem.title: USA: Georgian diplomat surrenders over accident charges.
newsitem.headline: Georgian diplomat surrenders over accident charges.

text.p: A Georgian diplomat turned himself in to authorities on Thursday to face criminal charges over his role in an auto accident that killed a 16-year-old girl in Washington last month, federal law enforcement officials said.

They said the diplomat, Gueorgui Makharadze, would be formally charged on Thursday with involuntary manslaughter and four counts of aggravated assault, charges which carry a maximum punishment of 70 years in prison.

Police have said speed and alcohol may have played a role in the five-car crash on Jan. 4, allegedly triggered when Makharadze, travelling at an estimated 80 miles per hour (129 kph), slammed into a car stopped for a red light at Dupont Circle in the heart of Washington. The accident killed Joviane Waltrick, a Brazilian girl living in Kensington, Maryland.
"He has turned himself in," one official said. "He is in the process of being charged right now."

The officials said Makharadze would be processed by the police, having his fingerprints taken, and an arraignment had been set for later in the day in a local court. U.S. Attorney Eric Holder scheduled a news conference to announce the charges.
Georgia has formally waived diplomatic immunity for Makharadze. The officials said prosecutors wanted him to surrender his passport but he probably would be released on certain conditions.
